protocol.question: Does first-batch GPU dispatch before query staging reduce fresh-query operation duration versus the existing streaming pool and matched dispatch-after-staging controls?
protocol.orderScheme: Williams 6 rows; 12 measured trials = two balanced blocks; positions and directed predecessors balanced within trials
protocol.timed: Fresh owned query snapshot from already parsed cloud, query staging and full chosen pipeline, ordered f64 summaries, f32 export, acknowledged query release and output transfer
protocol.excluded: File parsing, reference imports, device initialization, correctness oracles and diagnostic f64 exports
protocol.defaultChangeGate: No production/default change in this increment; evaluate all four reports against streaming and matched controls before considering integration
protocol.safety: Reuse verified compiled production and experimental WASM; no Rust rebuilds or toolchain downloads; no adapter identity; preserve all trials and tails; no heavy work during timing; original maps unchanged; dispatch timestamps describe host scheduling and do not prove GPU execution concurrency

limitations: Already loaded query cloud; file parsing and initial reference cache preparation excluded.
Six modes coexist; committed WASM pages are not isolated application RSS.
Release acknowledgements are awaited for this experiment; the normal application schedules pool releases asynchronously.
Fixed-hint and GPU pipelines have different timing scopes; do not pool them.
Median paired ratios need not equal a ratio of separate medians. All raw trials and long waits are retained.
Repeated fresh snapshots use the same measured cloud coordinates; no scene-change or SLAM accuracy claim.
Host offsets verify API-call order, not hardware execution timestamps or shader duration.
No production integration, recovery, cancellation, automatic selection or default change.
